lines.name: Pieces of the Past
lines.about: A Daedric quest for Mehrunes Dagon: Silus Vesuius of Dawnstar pays you to gather the three pieces of Mehrunes' Razor from Dead Crone Rock in the Reach, Cracked Tusk Keep in Falkreath and a house in Morthal, then meet him at the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon. It is one quest with a second, optional quest that lets you reforge the Razor yourself at a forge.

getIn.how: Talk to Silus in Dawnstar; he hires you to bring him the three pieces of Mehrunes' Razor for gold and gives you the details inside his house.

order.what: You recover the pommel from Drascua at Dead Crone Rock, the blade shards from Ghunzul at Cracked Tusk Keep and the hilt from Jorgen in Morthal, hand each to Silus, then meet him at the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon and speak to Mehrunes Dagon.
order.where: Dawnstar and the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon, the Pale

order.what: Silus agrees to let you reforge the Razor yourself at any forge, after which you can keep it or give it to him for a reward.
order.where: any forge (the records mark the Dawnstar forge)
order.needs: Ask Silus while you are still gathering the pieces, before he has all three; the log asks for skill in working with both enchanted and Daedric materials.

options: Kill Silus for Mehrunes Dagon: Dagon reforges the Razor and it is yours.
Refuse to kill Silus: the Razor is out of your grasp for good.
Reforge the Razor yourself with Silus's leave, which starts Reforging the Past.
Give the reforged Razor to Silus for a reward.
Keep the Razor.

gives: Gold from Silus for the pieces
closes: Silus Vesuius dies if you side with Mehrunes Dagon
Refusing Dagon at the shrine leaves the Razor out of your reach
Pieces of the Past fails if Silus dies before the end

unsure.why: No level gate shows on Pieces of the Past in the records (no start conditions, starts with the game), so the level it is made for isn't given.
The opening log suggests you first meet Silus outside his house, but his packages only place him inside it and around his home.
Reforging the Past's skill need isn't tied to named perks or a skill level in the records, and its opening line's words aren't in the files.
How much gold Silus pays for the pieces, and what his 'substantial reward' for the reforged Razor is, aren't in the records.
Whether taking the Reforging the Past route ends the Shrine of Mehrunes Dagon part of Pieces of the Past isn't shown.

lines.name: Saints and Seducers
lines.about: A Shivering Isles story: a quake leads you to Staada, a Golden Saint in the Solitude Wasteworks, who takes you to the Isles to put down a prisoners' riot at the Asylum and hunt their leader Thoron. The line holds three story quests and four side jobs in the Isles, two of which teach you to smith madness ore and amber and two of which give you an Elytra pet.

getIn.where: the Solitude Wasteworks, through a strange tunnel reached from the Solitude Sewers
getIn.how: The quest starts on its own when you feel a quake; investigate it and the strange tunnel to meet Staada, who then asks you to come with her to the Asylum in The Isle of Madness.

order.what: Sees-the-Moon, an Argonian in the marsh, sends you to the Drowned Ruin for his treasure and gives you his journal, which teaches you to work madness ore.
order.needs: Be in the Shivering Isles, which The Isle of Madness takes you to.

order.what: You follow a quake down a strange tunnel and meet Staada.
You help Staada fight off the rioting prisoners at the Asylum, rescue Dylora and defeat Thoron, who escapes.
order.where: the Asylum and Stopgap, Shivering Isles
order.needs: Meet Staada in The Route of Madness.

order.what: Staada sends you for an artifact from the Shivering Isles to break Thoron's amber barrier, and you defeat him in the Root Nexus.
order.where: Borogove and the Root Nexus, Shivering Isles

order.what: Theodor Gorlash teaches you to smith amber in return for the Sheogorath-Shaped Amber from the Root Canal.
order.where: The Near Corgi Shop and the Root Canal, Shivering Isles

order.what: You free a caged Elytra nymph named Potema, who becomes your pet.
You free a caged Elytra nymph named Pelagius, who becomes your pet.

options: Bring Nerveshatter from the ruins of Borogove.
Bring another artifact from the Shivering Isles; Dylora can point you to others.
Optional tasks: burn the Grove of Insanity or the laboratory, steal a Soul Tomato or a Void Essence, and frame the Priests or the Apostles.

gives: Spell Tome: Conjure Staada, a Master-level Conjuration spell
The knowledge to smith madness ore (Sees-the-Moon's Journal)
The knowledge to smith amber (Amber Smithing Manual)
Potema and Pelagius, Elytra nymph pets
closes: The Lunatic's Treasure fails if Sees-the-Moon is killed

unsure.why: No level gate or start condition for The Route of Madness is decoded in the records (it starts on a change-of-location event), so the level it is made for isn't given.
Which place fires The Route of Madness and whether it checks level or anything else isn't in the files.

That the Solitude Wasteworks is reached from the Solitude Sewers is read from its doors only; some of those doors stay hidden until the quest switches them on, and the records file the Wasteworks under the Shivering Isles.
The line's record order puts The Lunatic's Treasure first, but it needs you in the Shivering Isles, which The Isle of Madness takes you to; the story starts with The Route of Madness.
How the two Elytra pet quests start (finding the cage, taking the key or seeing the nymph) isn't in the records, nor the exact spots of the cages.
Conjure Staada and Staada's Helmet are properties of The Roots of Madness's script; the closing log names neither, so who receives them isn't confirmed. The helmet is left out for that reason.
The Merchant's Masterpiece's script also holds a Ring of Disrobing; nothing confirms you are given it.
What the optional burning, stealing and framing tasks change, and who gives them, isn't in the records.

lines.name: The Taste of Death
lines.about: A Daedric quest for Namira set in Markarth and Reachcliff Cave in the Reach: you look into the closed Hall of the Dead and meet Eola, who invites you into her coven of cannibals. Markarth's talk about the Hall waits until level 20, and the line has three quests, the last of which turns against the coven instead.

getIn.quest: Investigate the Hall of the Dead
getIn.where: Understone Keep, Markarth (otherwise he keeps the Hall of the Dead)
getIn.how: The quest begins on its own in Markarth; speak to Brother Verulus about the Hall of the Dead, which Kleppr and Frabbi at the Silver-Blood Inn also mention as a rumour.
needs: Character level 20 for the Markarth rumours that point you to the Hall of the Dead

order.quest: Investigate the Hall of the Dead
order.what: You speak to Brother Verulus, investigate the Hall of the Dead and tell him it is safe.
order.where: Understone Keep and the Hall of the Dead, Markarth

order.what: Eola, whom you meet in the Hall of the Dead, asks you to clear Reachcliff Cave of draugr, then lure Brother Verulus to the Shrine of Namira, kill him and feast.
Reading Eola's Journal sends you to Reachcliff Cave for evidence and to the Jarl of Markarth, and you confront the cannibals Hogni Red-Arm, Lisbet and Banning.
order.needs: Eola's Journal, taken from Eola after she attacks you.

options: Turn Eola down; she waits outside Reachcliff Cave if you change your mind.
Kill Eola; the quest fails and her journal can start A Bitter Aftertaste.
Lead Verulus to the shrine, kill him and feast to join the coven.
Confront the cannibals without the Jarl's leave; the log warns this may be unlawful.
Get the Jarl of Markarth's permission first, then deal with them as you see fit or have them arrested.

gives: A reward from the Jarl of Markarth at the end of A Bitter Aftertaste
closes: Brother Verulus dies if you join the coven
Killing Verulus anywhere but the Shrine of Namira fails The Taste of Death
Hogni Red-Arm, Lisbet and Banning are killed or, for Hogni and Lisbet, jailed in Cidhna Mine on the A Bitter Aftertaste path

unsure.why: The level 20 check sits on Kleppr's and Frabbi's rumour lines; whether Investigate the Hall of the Dead itself, or Eola's opening line, waits for that level isn't shown.
The quest starts on a change-location event; which location fires it isn't in the files. The Hall of the Dead door is Adept-locked and Verulus carries the key; whether he hands it over isn't shown.
What makes Eola attack you, which leads to A Bitter Aftertaste, isn't in the records; the log only speaks of 'the cannibal who assaulted me'.
The Taste of Death's script also holds gold and Invisibility; the records don't confirm either is given to you. What the Jarl gives at the end of A Bitter Aftertaste isn't named.
Eola is in the potential-follower group and has a greeting for after the quest, so she may offer to follow you once you join the coven; the records don't confirm it.
The Amulet of Arkay is held by Investigate the Hall of the Dead's script; that it comes when you tell Verulus the Hall is safe is read from the objective order.
What happens to Banning if he is arrested isn't shown; only Hogni Red-Arm and Lisbet have jailed copies in Cidhna Mine.

lines.name: The Whispering Door
lines.about: A Daedric quest for Mephala in Dragonsreach, Whiterun: Jarl Balgruuf asks you to find out what is wrong with his son Nelkir, which leads to a whispering door and the Ebony Blade. The line has two quests, the second of which asks whether you keep the Blade or destroy it.

getIn.how: Talk to Jarl Balgruuf and he asks you to find out what is wrong with Nelkir; Nelkir, Frothar and Dagny also have lines that lead into it.

order.what: You listen to the Whispering Door, get its key, open it and take the Ebony Blade, either by following Mephala through Nelkir or by warning the Jarl.

order.quest: The Fate of the Ebony Blade
order.what: Once you hold the Ebony Blade you decide whether to keep it or cast it into the fires of the Aetherium Forge.

options: Follow Mephala: talk to Nelkir and open the door, and take the Ebony Blade.
Warn the Jarl, then report to Balgruuf and hand the Blade to a Vigilant of Stendarr to be rid of it.
Keep the Blade and kill allies with it to restore it to its full potential.

branches.at: The Fate of the Ebony Blade
options: Keep the Blade and set out to restore it.
Destroy it in the Aetherium Forge and be freed of its dark magic.

gives: Ebony Blade (greatsword), restored to full power after you kill allies with it
closes: The Ebony Blade, if you give it to a Vigilant of Stendarr or destroy it in the Aetherium Forge
The allies you kill to restore the Blade

unsure.why: No level gate shows on the Jarl's or Nelkir's opening lines in the records, so the level it is made for isn't given.
The Whispering Door - Quest Expansion changes the opening dialogue's conditions, including a check tied to the Imperial side of the civil war; what that check does for a player isn't decoded.
Nelkir's family has a Blue Palace package for when the Jarl is exiled in the civil war; in that case they would be in Solitude.
Who holds the Whispering Door key isn't shown.

The Aetherium Forge door stays hidden until a Dawnguard enable parent is switched on, and the Forge belongs to Lost to the Ages; you probably need that quest's progress to get in, but the records don't say outright.

lines.name: Wyrmstooth
lines.about: A dragon hunt for the East Empire Company's Lurius Liore that starts in Whiterun and Falkreath and moves to the island of Wyrmstooth, reached by ship from Solitude. It opens at level 20, has two story quests, and the island holds a fort you can buy plus many side jobs and bounties.

getIn.where: he walks up to you wherever you are; otherwise he waits in the Bannered Mare in Whiterun
getIn.how: Once you reach level 20 the Imperial courier Theodyn Bienne finds you and tells you to speak to Lurius Liore at the Bannered Mare about trouble with a dragon.

order.what: Athir asks you to get his sword Embersunder back from the Forsworn at Hag's End.
Lurius sails you and the mercenaries to Wyrmstooth, where you go through Wyrmstooth Barrow into Dimfrost, the dragon's den, and defend Stonehollow from Vulthurkrah.
order.where: Solitude docks, then Stonehollow, Wyrmstooth Barrow and Dimfrost on Wyrmstooth

order.what: Fjeimir's letter sends you to take the cache key from Rolgar's body in Dimfrost and open Blind Robber's Cache.
order.where: Dimfrost and Blind Robber's Bluff, Wyrmstooth
order.needs: Reach Dimfrost, which Barrow of the Wyrm takes you into.

order.what: A bounty job: kill the bear south of Fort Valus.
A bounty job: kill the Marauder Clanlord at Cragwater Cavern.
A bounty job: kill the Master Vampire at Bloodfrost Burrow.
A bounty job: kill the troublesome warlock at Krakevisa, north of Stonehollow.
Daenlit asks you to steal an enchanted necklace that Erikur keeps in Solitude.
Lurius Liore hires you to hunt the dragon Vulthurkrah with his mercenaries; you fight it at Ancient's Ascent and tell Lurius it fled to Wyrmstooth.
order.where: The Bannered Mare, Whiterun, and Ancient's Ascent, Falkreath

order.what: Elmera asks you for 30 spiddal sticks from the Deadlands.
order.needs: Meet Elmera among Lurius's mercenaries, and a way into the Deadlands.

order.what: Alberthor asks you to kill the Thalmor spies in Haetar's Cave.
order.needs: Reach Alberthor in Wyrmstooth Barrow, which Barrow of the Wyrm opens.

order.what: You find the abandoned Fort Valus, buy its deed from Lurius Liore and pay him for upgrades and a crew.
order.where: Fort Valus and the East Empire Company Tradehouse, Wyrmstooth
order.needs: Be on Wyrmstooth with Lurius there.

order.what: Bolmar asks you to deal with the spriggans in Gronndal Grove, where the miners have dug into a spriggan sanctuary.
Shargam asks you to sail back to Skyrim and kill Ulfgar at the Silver-Blood Inn in Markarth.
Signy asks you to steal the ledger in which Erikur of Solitude keeps her father's debt.
Gjalrunn, paralysed and robbed in the wilds, asks you to get back the golden pants a witch stole; you chase them to Krakevisa.
order.needs: A daedra heart if you want Glendora's antidote for him.

order.what: A voice in the Tomb of Vulom asks you to bring back his bones, and once you do he rises as a lich you must destroy.
The wounded tracker Dunyick asks you to find his wolf Faelor and kill the marauders who attacked him.
Alberthor asks you for 8 wisp wrappings.

options: Kill the Spriggan Matriarch and clear the grove for the miners.
Side with the Matriarch and kill the miners who got away.
Agree to help the Matriarch, then betray her and clear the grove.
Give the golden pants to Glendora the witch for a reward.
Give the pants back to Gjalrunn.
Keep the pants and lie to him.
Trade Glendora a daedra heart for the paralysis antidote and free him.
Tell him there is no cure; he asks you to end his misery.
Send Faelor home to Dunyick's camp.
Take Faelor along as a companion.

gives: Fort Valus, bought from Lurius Liore, with upgrades and a hired crew
Faelor the wolf as a companion
Athir, Daenlit, Elmera and Shargam can follow you
A reward from Lurius Liore at the end of Barrow of the Wyrm
closes: Siding with the miners in A Priceless Commodity means killing the Spriggan Matriarch; siding with the spriggans means killing the Gronndal miners
Ulfgar dies in Repaying a Debt
Dunyick dies of his wounds in A Howl Load of Trouble
Gjalrunn dies if you put him out of his misery in The Naked Nord

unsure.why: The line's record order is not story order. The story runs Wyrmstooth, then Barrow of the Wyrm; most of the other quests need you on the island, which the records only show you reaching on the Red Wave during Barrow of the Wyrm.
How the four bounty jobs are handed out isn't in the records; the island has a 'Check the notice board for work' pointer, so they are probably taken from a notice board.
Whether the mercenaries' and Alberthor's favours are offered during the story or only after Barrow of the Wyrm isn't shown; their opening lines only check that the quest hasn't begun.
Stickler in the Mud only names the Deadlands; The Cause is the only quest in the files that takes you there, and whether you must finish it or only reach its Oblivion Gate isn't shown.
For Robbed Blind the records place Erikur in his house in Solitude and mark a coffin of his as holding the necklace, but the coffin's spot isn't in the files.
The records give enemy levels but not a level the island is made for: Wyrmstooth Barrow 24-60, Dimfrost 24-79, Bloodfrost Burrow's boss 55-125, Vulom level 51.
Lurius's reward for Barrow of the Wyrm, the price of Fort Valus and its upgrades, and most side-job rewards aren't named in the records.

No dialogue or event in the files starts Wyrmstooth; the courier's walk-to-you package needs the quest already running and your level at or above 20 (raised from 10 by a Requiem patch). Whether Theodyn gives the message below level 20 if you find him yourself isn't shown.
